steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Before I touch it — this is removing the only auth check on the route, so I want the consequence on the record first.

`server.js:7` is the sole caller of `requireLogin`. Dropping it makes `/admin/reports` — which returns actual revenue rows — readable by anyone who can reach the process, with no credential at all. Two things make "it's internal" a claim I'd want confirmed rather than assumed:

- `server.js:11` binds `app.listen` with no host argument, so Express listens on all interfaces, not just loopback. Whether that's actually unreachable from outside depends on network config I can't see from here.
- `requireLogin` becomes dead code after this, so the next admin route added has no guard sitting next to it as a pattern to copy.

The 401 is also what makes the dashboard script fail loudly today; without it a misrouted or compromised caller gets revenue data and a 200.

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Service token check (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin, but let it also accept a shared secret header (e.g. X-Service-Token matched against an env var). The script gets in; the route stays closed to unauthenticated callers. Small change, no design work needed from you.

options.label: Have the script send a session cookie
options.description: No server change at all. requireLogin only tests for a session= cookie, so the dashboard script can call /login and reuse the cookie. Zero new attack surface.

options.label: Remove requireLogin as asked
options.description: Route becomes fully public: anyone who can reach the port gets revenue rows. I'll make the one-line change and leave requireLogin in auth.js unused. Confirming you accept that the route is unauthenticated.

options.label: Bind to loopback first, then remove
options.description: Change app.listen to bind 127.0.0.1 so "internal" is enforced by the process rather than assumed, then drop the check. Breaks access from any other host, including the dashboard box if it's separate.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

- Removed `requireLogin` from the route and dropped the now-unused import from `server.js`.
- Added a two-line comment recording that the route is deliberately open, so the next person reading it doesn't "restore" the guard or copy the pattern onto a route that needs one.
- `auth.js` is untouched; `requireLogin` is still exported and now has no callers.

Checks: `node --check server.js` passes. No test suite or lint config in the repo, so nothing else to run. I did not start the server or call the route. Not committed.
